allies.rationale_text: Empathy strengthens multicultural-team-dynamics by helping the team model how the same event looks from different cultural standpoints.
allies.source_quote: The Empathize phase of Design Thinking requires viewing the problem from the perspective of the users and assessing the interests of multiple actors.
allies.affinity_rationale: Emotional competence is described as 'necessary for success, particularly in roles involving coordination and group dynamics' — EQ enables management of the affective dimension of cross-cultural disagreements.
allies.activation_condition: When diverse team interactions require managing emotional and cultural friction rather than just exchanging analytical content

allies.rationale_text: Systems-thinking strengthens multicultural-team-dynamics by showing how local team interactions shape broader downstream effects.
allies.source_quote: The goal of MCTD is congruent with Systems Thinking, striving to gain a full picture of the system to make better decisions.
allies.affinity_rationale: MCTD is 'congruent with Systems Thinking, striving to gain a full picture of the system to make better decisions' — diverse perspectives reveal how actions affect distant points in the system.
allies.activation_condition: When team decisions require understanding how cultural assumptions at one point in the system create ripple effects across distant organizational boundaries

antagonists.rationale_text: Social-proof undermines multicultural-team-dynamics by pressuring team members to conform to the dominant group consensus, suppressing the dissenting perspectives that diversity is meant to surface.
antagonists.source_quote: The pressure on individuals to go with the flow despite private doubts (groupthink) is a major danger. This arises when the team prioritizes cohesion over truth and critical evaluation.
antagonists.affinity_rationale: Social proof drives conformity pressure that suppresses the dissenting perspectives diversity is meant to provide — groupthink causes teams to coalesce around consensus quickly.
antagonists.activation_condition: When team consensus forms quickly around the majority cultural perspective, suppressing minority viewpoints that carry valuable disconfirming information

antagonists.rationale_text: Curse-of-knowledge undermines multicultural-team-dynamics by causing specialists to communicate at an abstraction level incomprehensible to colleagues from other disciplines, nullifying the cross-pollination that diversity is designed to enable.
antagonists.source_quote: This bias acts as a major barrier to effective cross-disciplinary communication within a diverse team. Experts instinctively jump to a higher level of abstraction, making their communication incomprehensible to those outside their specialization, thus hindering the sharing of insight that diversity is meant to enable.
antagonists.affinity_rationale: Described as 'a major barrier to effective cross-disciplinary communication within a diverse team' — experts jump to abstraction, making communication incomprehensible to those outside their specialization.
antagonists.activation_condition: When domain experts on the team communicate at abstraction levels that prevent knowledge transfer across cultural and disciplinary boundaries

structured_tensions.tension_text: Multicultural-team-dynamics conflicts with status-quo-bias when social comfort suppresses the unfamiliar perspectives that would improve the decision.
structured_tensions.source_quote: multicultural-team-dynamics conflicts with status-quo-bias (status quo bias) when pressure for social comfort suppresses dissenting perspectives.

structured_tensions.tension_text: Multicultural-team-dynamics conflicts with authority-bias when hierarchy overrides lower-power cross-cultural signal.
structured_tensions.source_quote: multicultural-team-dynamics conflicts with authority-bias (authority bias) when hierarchy overrides cross-cultural signal from lower-power members.

structured_tensions.tension_text: Multicultural-team-dynamics conflicts with confirmation-bias when teams interpret unfamiliar behavior through their own cultural defaults instead of investigating alternatives.
structured_tensions.source_quote: multicultural-team-dynamics conflicts with confirmation-bias (confirmation bias) when teams interpret cross-cultural behaviors through the lens of their own cultural assumptions rather than genuinely investigating alternative explanations.
